Maria Ortiz: Heads-up — onboarding a new 70B variant. Weights staged at s3://rw-inference/weights/70b-qs-2026/. Two immediate concerns: RoPE scaling (model trained with scaled RoPE x1.4 but model_config.rope_scale=1.0) and tokenizer looks like SentencePiece with slightly different BOS/EOS tokens. Plan: serve with MQA enabled. Need quick checks on sliding-window chunking, kv-cache layout, and any runtime flags. Can someone confirm the minimal config we should use for a canary?

Samir Patel: @Maria I'll take this. Can you paste the model config + tokenizer.json or a snippet? Also which quantization target — 8bit or 4bit? That changes kernel selection.

Maria Ortiz: Pasting trimmed config below (removed large arrays):
```json
{
  "model": "70b-qs-2026",
  "architecture": "decoder-only",
  "d_model": 12288,
  "n_heads": 96,
  "rope_scale": 1.0,
  "gqa": false,
  "mqa": true,
  "tokenizer": "sentencepiece",
  "vocab_file": "tokenizer.model"
}
```
Tokenizer notes: merges unknowns to <unk>, and our default tokenizer pipeline expects `padding_side=right` and `add_bos=false`. This one sets add_bos=true at encode time.

Samir Patel: Ok. Two immediate action items:
1) RoPE: runtime supports an override key `runtime.overrides.rope_scale`. Set to `1.4` and run the runtime unit test `tests/unit/rope_scaling_test.py`. That should catch any rotary phase drift.
2) Tokenizer: we need a small adapter that rewrites `add_bos=true` to false for serving, or change the model config `tokenizer.add_bos=false` if that matches training preprocessing. Quick workaround: `tokenizer_adapter: { add_bos: false, normalize: true }`.

Li Wei: Re: MQA/GQA — model's head layout looks like MQA (n_heads=96, but per-key/query groups in metadata indicate multi-query). Runtime expects `attention.layout=mqa` when `mqa=true`. If you set `mqa=true` but runtime kernel picks GQA kernels you will see correctness failures at long context because kv cache indexing differs. So explicitly set `runtime.attention.layout = "mqa"`.

Nate H: I ran the lightweight verify script against a local extract (not full weights):
```bash
./tools/verify_onboard.sh s3://rw-inference/weights/70b-qs-2026/ --rope 1.4 --mqa --tokenizer-path ./tokenizer.model
```
Output excerpt: `OK: forward pass small batch (seq=512)`
But there was a warning: `KV_CACHE_ALIGN: detected stride mismatch, falling back to safe copy (perf hit)`. That usually means the serialized key-value layout didn't match the runtime packing settings.

Olga K: For serving config: set `sliding_window.max_context` to 4096 only if the model was trained for that. Safer default is 2048 with `sliding_window.overlap=128`. Also set `runtime.kv_stride=64` to match upstream packing if you saw the stride mismatch. For A40 small ded pools with MQA enabled, cap `batch_limit` at 8 to avoid OOMs.

Jen Torres: CI/QA note: add a short eval suite with these cases:
- long-prefix alignment (seq 2048 -> seq 4096)
- repeated prompt with BOS toggled both ways (add_bos true/false)
- quantization smoke (fp16 vs 4bit)
This will catch tokenization and kv-cache offset bugs early.

Samir Patel: Also, small config snippet to include in PR for canary (copy into runtime config):
```yaml
model: 70b-qs-2026
runtime:
  overrides:
    rope_scale: 1.4
  attention:
    layout: mqa
  kv_stride: 64
sliding_window:
  max_context: 2048
  overlap: 128
tokenizer_adapter:
  add_bos: false
  normalization: true
serve_limits:
  batch_limit: 8
  max_tokens_per_minute: 50000
```

deploy-bot: Canary start queued for model=70b-qs-2026 on ded-pool-3 at 2026-11-05T14:03:10Z. (status: queued)

Maria Ortiz: Awesome, thanks. I'll update the PR with Samir's snippet and add the eval prompts Jen suggested. I'll also push a tokenizer adapter patch to our tokenizer service. Will ping again when PR is merged so someone can kick the canary. :thumbsup: :eyes:
